question: What does a network of permutation contact remember once its witnesses are forgotten, can its loops bind into knots, and which kinds of local reasoning fail to see that a network is impossible?

definitions.network: a connected simple graph with oriented edges; a witness with values W = {0..n-1} at every vertex; on every edge a link: a middle variable whose each value m names a permutation p_m of W, and the copy allows (w_u, m, w_v) exactly when w_v = p_m(w_u)
definitions.composite: the relation on the middle variables obtained by forgetting every witness: a pattern is allowed when some witness assignment satisfies every copy
definitions.holonomy: for a pattern, fix a BFS spanning tree rooted at vertex 0 and let g_v be the composed permutation along the tree path from the root to v; the fundamental holonomy of a non-tree edge u->v is g_v^-1 p g_u; the holonomy group H is generated by the fundamental holonomies
definitions.regular group link: the middle variable ranges over a permutation group G on W and names itself
definitions.selector bouquet: k triangles r-x_i-y_i-r sharing the root r; edges r->x_i and x_i->y_i carry fixed decoy permutations drawn at random; edge y_i->r carries a two-valued selector s_i chosen so that loop i has holonomy identity when s_i = 0 and h_i when s_i = 1
definitions.shape: the free-set complex of a relation: the sets of variables on which it allows every assignment
definitions.nerve: the sets S of loops whose holonomies h_i (i in S) share a fixed point
definitions.knot among loops: a set S of at least three loops that is a minimal non-face of the nerve; a tie is a minimal non-face of two loops
definitions.level-k affine relaxation over R: variables z[S,f] for every set S of at most k vertices and every assignment f of S that satisfies the copies with both ends in S; equations z[{}] = 1 and z[S,f] = sum of z[S+v,f'] over the extensions f' of f; feasible when it has a solution with entries in R
definitions.pinned level-2 relaxation: the level-2 relaxation plus z[{r},w] = 1 if w = u else 0, for a base value u
definitions.arc consistency: prune witness values without a supporting value across some edge, until stable
definitions.path consistency: (2,3)-consistency: keep a relation for every pair of vertices, intersect it with every composition through a third vertex until stable; refute when one becomes empty

public_inputs.graphs: C3, C4, C5, C6; theta (vertices 0,1,a,b,c with three paths 0-x-1); K4; K_{2,3}; triangular prism; bouquets of two and three triangles at one vertex
public_inputs.group_links: Z2 on 2 values, Z3 on 3, S3 on 3, C6 = <(01)(234)> on 5 on graphs with at most 6 edges, S4 on 4 on graphs with at most 4 edges, Z2 and Z3 also on the 9-edge graphs; every pattern
public_inputs.random_links: on every graph, n in {3,4,5}: 10 assignments of two random permutations per edge (seed 20261019); every pattern
public_inputs.selector_bouquets: k loops, n values: every holonomy tuple for (2,3), (2,4), (3,3), (3,4); 3000 sampled tuples for (3,5), (4,4) and (4,5); decoys from seed 20261019
public_inputs.complexes: every simplicial complex (down-set containing the empty face) on k = 1..4 labelled vertices
public_inputs.size_bound: every k-tuple of permutations of k values for k = 2, 3, 4; the star transpositions (j k) on k+1 values
public_inputs.local_reasoning: rings C3-C6 with a holonomy of every cycle type on n = 2..5 values, gauge randomized; theta, K4 and the two-triangle bouquet with declared holonomy tuples, including (01),(234) on 5 values and the star transpositions (03),(13),(23) on 4; rings F2, F3, Q, Z

forbidden_inputs: holonomy, fixed points or orbit sizes as inputs to the producer's composite, shape or linear-system computations

predictions.P1: every composite allows a pattern exactly when the fundamental holonomies share a fixed point
predictions.P2: with a regular group link G the allowed count is |G|^E * sum over nonempty T of (-1)^(|T|+1) (|G_T|/|G|)^b1, where G_T fixes T pointwise and b1 = E - V + 1; it depends on the graph only through b1; for Z2 and Z3 it is |G|^(E - b1)
predictions.P3: the shape of every selector-bouquet composite is the nerve of the holonomies' fixed-point sets; every minimal non-face of three or more loops passes knotlab's K1-K3 check and excludes only the all-ones pattern on its loops; when every h_i is the identity or has no fixed point there is no tie or knot
predictions.P4: (a) every complex on at most four vertices is the shape of the bouquet with W = its facets plus two points and h_i one cycle through the facets missing i and the two points; (b) no k-tuple of permutations of k values is a knot among k loops (every k-1 share a fixed point, all k do not), for k = 2, 3, 4, and the star transpositions on k+1 values are one
predictions.P5: (a) the level-2 relaxation over R accepts exactly when 1 is in the ideal of R generated by the sizes of the H-orbits; (b) pinned at u it accepts exactly when u is a common fixed point; (c) the level-3 relaxation over F2, F3 and Q refutes every impossible instance and accepts every possible one; (d) arc consistency refutes nothing, path consistency refutes exactly the impossible instances
predictions.P6: for Z2 and Z3 links the composite of a two-loop network is a function of the cycle types of the two loop holonomies; for S3 and S4 links it is not: some allowed and some excluded patterns have the same pair of cycle types

primary_observable: per instance: allowed counts and excluded patterns, shapes, minimal non-faces with knotlab verdicts, feasibility verdicts with a certificate (a solution or a refutation) for each ring and relaxation, and the agreement of each with its prediction
cheapest_meaningful_control: (1) The composite is computed by backtracking search over witness values, never from holonomy. (2) Every linear-algebra verdict carries a certificate: a solution, or a combination of equations that reads 0 = 1 (mod p for F_p and for Z-refutations). (3) A non-permutation link (one allowing two values out of one value in) must be able to break P1. (4) The prediction with 'some' in place of 'all' in P5(c) must be distinguishable: level 2 over Q must accept some impossible instance.
independent_check: check_result.py rebuilds every system and network with separate code, verifies every certificate by substitution, recomputes composites by the covering-graph criterion (a component of the label-extended graph that meets every vertex once), recomputes shapes and re-derives every predicted value
decision_or_followup_rule: A signal is P1-P6 holding on every declared case. A signal supports tickets B and C, which carry the proofs; any mismatch is a counterexample to the theory and stops the affected ticket until it is understood.
first_executable_signal: P1 and P2 on rings and the theta graph, then selectors, complexes, local reasoning
stop_rule: Stop after the declared roster; stop early only on a solver or control failure.
notes: Before this freeze, the planning-stage claim that level-k relaxations with k below the loop's length accept an impossible ring exactly when 1 is in the orbit-size ideal was withdrawn: a three-witness walk refutes every impossible ring. Rings of length 4 to 6 at level 3 discriminate the two claims.
nonclaims: Finite enumeration on the declared graphs, contacts, rings and instances; the general statements are tickets B and C.
Permutation contact only; links that are not permutations appear only as a control.
No claim about Nullstellensatz degree, cohomological k-consistency at higher levels, or the complexity of any CSP class.
No claim about native loops, space, distance or physics.
